long_biography.plain_text:
Philip S. Niarchos is the eldest son of Greek shipping magnate Stavros Niarchos, whose tanker fleet created the family fortune and financed a major collection of modern art. Philip inherited much of that collection after his father's death in 1996, then broadened it with post-war and contemporary works by artists including Andy Warhol, Jean-Michel Basquiat and Maurizio Cattelan.

Forbes now identifies the art collection itself as his source of wealth. Niarchos is a trustee of the Museum of Modern Art and co-president of the Stavros Niarchos Foundation, linking private collecting with cultural stewardship and philanthropy. The family's 115.8-metre Atlantis II, commissioned by his father at Hellenic Shipyards in 1981 and retained after his death, provides a surviving connection to the shipping era from which the collection grew.
